_meta.system: You are an expert music analyst.
_meta.judge_template:
You hear FOUR short clips from a DJ's track library, presented in order: clip A first, then clip B, then clip C, then clip D.

This question is about a single perceptual dimension: {axis_id}.
- LOW pole:  {low_pole}
- HIGH pole: {high_pole}

For each clip, decide where it sits on the LOW ↔ HIGH scale, then ORDER all four clips from CLOSEST to LOW pole (least toward HIGH) to CLOSEST to HIGH pole (most toward HIGH).

Reply with EXACTLY one line: four letters in order, lowest-pole first, no separator. Use each letter (A, B, C, D) exactly once.
Example: "BACD" means B is least toward HIGH, then A, then C, then D is most toward HIGH.

Then on a second line, one short justification (≤25 words).
_meta._pair_budget_rationale: 16 axes × 12000 K=4 calls = 192000 LLM calls. Each call yields 6 pair observations (4 choose 2) for ~72000 pair labels per axis. Bootstrap 20% uniform (2400 calls) + BALD 80% (9600 calls) per axis. Wall ~10 hr at 12 inflight, ~2.0 s per call. Coverage: ~8 games/track on the full 15314-track corpus. Replaces round-7 1500 pairwise pairs/axis on 1424 tracks.
_meta.convention: LOW pole = less intense / less aggressive end. HIGH pole = more intense / more aggressive end. The blend optimiser learns the sign at training time; the LOW→HIGH ordering is for human interpretability and prompt clarity, not for label sign.

axes.low_pole: clean, smooth tone with no distortion, fuzz, clipping, or saturation
axes.high_pole: distorted, fuzzy, heavily saturated or clipped tone
axes.rationale: non-linear processing on pitched material; replaces the round-7 'distortion' axis with explicit clean anti-pole

axes.low_pole: bright, uplifting, major-key, hopeful or joyful mood
axes.high_pole: dark, brooding, minor-key, ominous or shadowy mood
axes.rationale: tonal mood + frequency emphasis; round-7 darkness was the only non-redundant axis, polar form should keep it sharp

axes.low_pole: sparse texture: few elements, breathing room, minimalist arrangement
axes.high_pole: dense texture: many simultaneous layers, busy, packed arrangement
axes.rationale: number of concurrent voices; polar anti-pole separates 'busy' from 'loud'

axes.low_pole: steady pulse, four-on-the-floor, predictable subdivisions, on-grid
axes.high_pole: syncopated, breakbeat, polyrhythmic, displaced accents, off-grid
axes.rationale: groove complexity / syncopation; round-7 had real signal here

axes.low_pole: clean sung vocals OR no vocals OR melodic singing
axes.high_pole: shouted, screamed, growled, or harsh-effected vocals
axes.rationale: vocal performance intensity; absent-vocal tracks fall on the LOW pole by design

axes.low_pole: dynamic loudness with quiet-loud-quiet contrast and breathing room
axes.high_pole: flat, brick-walled, loudness-uniform, no dynamic rest
axes.rationale: loudness envelope / mastering; orthogonal to peak loudness

axes.low_pole: thin, light low-end with little or no sub-bass
axes.high_pole: heavy sub-bass and kick presence, chest-pushing low-end

axes.low_pole: relaxed, floating, slow-feeling regardless of measured BPM
axes.high_pole: urgent, frantic, fast-feeling regardless of measured BPM

axes.low_pole: tonal, singable, clear key, hummable melody
axes.high_pole: atonal, fragmented, no clear key, non-melodic
axes.rationale: pitch organisation; consolidates round-7 atonality + harmonic_dissonance with explicit singable anti-pole

axes.low_pole: intricate, through-composed, lots of melodic variation, harder to predict
axes.high_pole: simple, repetitive hook or riff, in-your-face, predictable
axes.rationale: user hypothesis: simple melody correlates with aggression (Prodigy / hardcore use simple riffs; jazz / prog use intricate ones)

axes.low_pole: purely pitched material, no noise or non-pitched FX layers
axes.high_pole: heavy non-pitched layers (white noise, hiss, noise FX, glitches)
axes.rationale: non-pitched sound design; distinct from timbre_roughness which is processing of pitched material

axes.low_pole: active chord changes, frequent modulations, harmonic movement
axes.high_pole: static drone, repeated chord, no harmonic motion
axes.rationale: harmonic stasis; flipped from intuition because static is the higher-intensity pole (peak techno, doom drone, hardstyle are all static)

axes.low_pole: continuous-energy flow, no buildup-and-drop structure, ambient or through-composed
axes.rationale: DJ-track form; very DJ-relevant, captures 'club banger' shape

axes.low_pole: lo-fi, raw, dusty, unpolished, tape-warm or rough mix
axes.rationale: production-era axis; orthogonal to most aggression-related axes, cross-library generalisation aid

axes.low_pole: organic acoustic instruments dominate (guitar, piano, drum kit, strings, voice)
axes.high_pole: synthetic, electronic, sampled, sound-design dominant (synths, drum machines, FX)
axes.rationale: instrument-source axis; captures acoustic vs electronic genre macro-structure

axes.low_pole: smooth, legato, few sharp transients, sustained tones
axes.rationale: attack vs sustain; distinct from rhythm_grid (subdivision) and from textural_density (number of voices)
